title: Pilot studies
question: What can a small pilot show, and what can it not?
placement: small pilots outside every leaderboard and model ranking
metric_units: balanced accuracy, AUROC, average precision, top-3 accuracy, shares and chance levels are proportions in [0,1]; differences of these are differences of proportions; the REFED error is a mean absolute error in raw label units on the published 1–255 scale (lower is better); counts of people, fields, folders, clips, runs, events, trials and channels are whole numbers; null means not computed or not stated, never zero
scope: Small pilots on four sources, all kept outside every leaderboard and model ranking. Published, each from its own approved aggregate export: one Orthosis cohort in three configurations, counted once; a cross-person, cross-language inner-speech baseline on BINGO; a mask-aware EEG analysis of a handwriting dataset; and a stored-clip computational diagnostic on REFED. No dataset, cohort, species, task or metric is pooled, and the results share no ranking.

pilots.label: Inner speech in Greek and English

orthosis-64ch-classical.title: Orthosis error events: the 64-channel classical baseline
orthosis-64ch-classical.question: Can a fixed EEG baseline tell injected orthosis errors from standard device events in a person it was not trained on?

configuration.label: 64-channel configuration
configuration.note: the first configuration of this cohort; it stays beside the 58-channel one

orthosis-64ch-classical.task: Recorded injected orthosis device errors against standard device events with no error introduced, from the 0–0.5 second window after each event. The labels describe recorded device events, not whether the person noticed the error.

cohort.counted_once: the same 8 people, 83 runs and 2,407 events in all three Orthosis results: one cohort, never counted twice in coverage
cohort.split: leave one whole person out: eight folds, all of a person’s runs held out together; the scaler and the probe are fitted on the other seven people

exclusions.note: baseline runs are not main-task runs; a target needs an observed following movement and a complete window

orthosis-64ch-classical.weighting: macro-person: the unweighted mean of the eight held-out people’s metrics, not pooled trial accuracy; balanced accuracy is not ordinary accuracy

eeg.label: Fixed EEG features + logistic regression, 64 channels
eeg.description: 576 fixed amplitude and log band-power values per event from 64 EEG channels; a training-only StandardScaler and a balanced L2 logistic regression with C=1, no tuning

confound.label: Direction/time confound probe
confound.description: the same fixed probe on movement direction, run order within the person, position in the run and time in the run: no EEG

majority.label: Training majority
majority.description: predicts the most frequent class of the seven training people

prior.label: Training class prior
prior.description: a constant probability, the error share of the seven training people

eeg_minus_confound.interval_note: no interval was computed for this difference

balanced_accuracy.range_is: the lowest and highest replicate means: an observed range, not a confidence interval

permutation_control.design: training labels shuffled within person and run, held-out labels untouched; a diagnostic control, not a full permutation significance test

response_clean_subset.status: secondary: counts only, never a headline
response_clean_subset.note: strongly label-selected and dominated by errors, so its high average precision is not comparable with the primary cohort and its scores are not published

method.signal: 64 EEG channels at 500 Hz with the declared header scaling; three acceleration channels excluded; the recorded reference kept
method.filter: continuous forward-only fourth-order Butterworth 1–30 Hz filtering that uses no future samples, zero state at each run start and a five-second warm-up
method.window: the complete half-open 0–0.5 second window after each event
method.probe: a training-only StandardScaler and a balanced L2 logistic regression; C=1 and the 0.5 decision rule fixed before execution; no tuning
method.eligibility: main-task runs only; inclusion does not depend on whether the person responded correctly
method.sealing: every fold and control prediction was sealed before a separate scorer read the held-out labels

uncertainty.kind: pointwise 95% percentile interval from 10,000 person-level bootstrap draws
uncertainty.limited_by: eight people give limited uncertainty estimation
uncertainty.conditional_on: the fixed sealed predictions; refitting is not included

orthosis-64ch-classical.reading: The fixed EEG baseline is above the direction/time confound probe, the class prior and every permutation control, with its interval clear of all three. It separates recorded device events; it does not show that the person recognised the error, and movement, muscle or device artifacts may contribute.
limitations: Eight people in one dataset: person-bootstrap uncertainty is limited, and this is not a population-level ranking.

The labels are recorded injected device events. The result does not show subjective error recognition, a mental state or isolated neural activity: movement, muscle and device-injection artifacts may contribute, and beating the direction/time confound probe does not isolate a neural origin.
The permutation controls shuffle training labels within person and run: diagnostic controls, not a full permutation significance test.

A response-clean subset of 451 events has only 5 standard events and 446 errors, and only three people have both classes. Its high average precision reflects that prevalence, so its scores are not published and it never replaces the primary result.
EEG only: no EMG model, fusion or paired EEG–EMG clock claim.
Offline, and a reanalysis by this site: not a reproduction of the authors’ competition score, and no real-time, clinical or state-of-the-art claim.
release_limits: Eight-person single-dataset pilot; person-bootstrap uncertainty is limited and is not a population-level ranking.
Labels describe recorded injected orthosis device events, not subjective recognition, mental states, clinical performance or isolated neural cognition.
EEG-only: no EMG model, multimodal fusion or paired EEG/EMG clock claim.
Movement, muscle, device-injection and other acquisition artifacts may contribute; the direction/time confound control does not isolate their origin.
Train-only within-person/run permutations are diagnostic controls, not a full dataset label-permutation significance test.
Response-clean secondary subset is strongly label-selected (446 error versus 5 correct events) and only three people have both classes; high AUPRC is not comparable to the primary population.
claims_not_supported: not subjective error recognition or isolated neural decoding
no real-time, online, clinical or deployment claim
not a population ranking and no state-of-the-art claim
no EMG, fusion or foundation-model result in this configuration

independent_audit.checked: all 384 score rows and 144 aggregate and interval rows recomputed from the sealed predictions, agreeing within 1e-12; twelve synthetic checks passed before execution
independent_audit.not_checked: no raw signal was read and no model was refitted

orthosis-eegpt-vs-58ch.reading: Frozen EEGPT with the fixed supervised probe is slightly below the matched 58-channel classical features on balanced accuracy, and the paired interval spans zero. This pilot establishes no advantage for either arm, and neither equivalence nor a general inferiority of EEG foundation models.
limitations: One short-window supervised transfer setup on eight people: the frozen encoder feeds a probe trained on the other seven people’s labels. Not zero-shot and not a verified unseen-dataset test.
The 64-channel classical scores were seen before this comparison was frozen: a prospective diagnostic, not a blind confirmatory comparison.
Montage, filtering, reference, scaling, population and the half-second, two-patch context differ from EEGPT’s pretraining; running it natively does not establish that the transfer suits it.

bingo-cross-language.title: Inner speech in Greek and English: across people and across languages
bingo-cross-language.question: Can a fixed spectral baseline trained on other people decode which of 15 nouns someone imagined saying, and does training in one language carry over to the other?
bingo-cross-language.task: 15-class classification of inner speech of 15 matched nouns in Greek and in English, from the 0–1.5 second inner-speech window that starts when the fixation cross appears; each source field is held out whole, both of its languages excluded from every fitted operation

cohort.counting_unit: source-defined subject fields: the operational groups; biological identity and cross-day grouping were not independently certified
cohort.incomplete_field: one incomplete field excluded by the prospective complete-record rule; no exclusion depended on a score

chance.note: balanced 15-class prior; top-3 prior is three in fifteen

bingo-cross-language.weighting: field-equal: the mean over the 17 held-out fields

balanced_accuracy.range_is: the lowest and highest replicate means: an observed range, not a confidence interval
the lowest and highest replicate means: an observed range, not a confidence interval
the lowest and highest replicate means: an observed range, not a confidence interval
the lowest and highest replicate means: an observed range, not a confidence interval

contrast.comparison: cross-language minus within-language balanced accuracy, the mean over the two training languages; the same held-out fields

greek.comparison: trained on Greek: tested on English minus tested on Greek

english.comparison: trained on English: tested on Greek minus tested on English

method.window: the stored time vectors verify the half-open 0–1.5 second action window at 300 Hz
method.inputs: per trial and channel, max-absolute scaling and demeaning, then Hann periodograms; four relative bands partition 1–30 Hz across 19 source-order channels; no guessed voltage calibration, montage interpolation or re-referencing
method.model: a source-only StandardScaler and RidgeClassifier with fixed alpha 1 and the Cholesky solver; no tuning against held-out scores; ties broken by a fixed noun order
method.controls: an order-only control, a high-frequency ratio control, the class prior and 20 training-label shuffles per direction
method.sealing: all 816 checkpoints sealed before any scoring

uncertainty.kind: approximate descriptive 2.5–97.5% intervals from 10,000 field bootstrap draws
uncertainty.conditional_on: fixed predictions from overlapping leave-one-field-out fits: training refit variability is omitted, and they are not calibrated population confidence intervals

protocol.source: BINGO deliverable D3.1, version 2.0, the cross-linguistic protocol (https://bingo-project.gr/download/397)

delivered_signal.statement: The project documents the same preprocessing for both of its released datasets: band-pass filtering from 1 to 145 Hz, notch filtering at 50 Hz and its harmonics, Artifact Subspace Reconstruction (ASR), FORCe removal of ocular and muscle artifacts, and then segmentation into trials. The signals analysed here were therefore artifact-cleaned on the continuous recordings before any trial was cut.
delivered_signal.source: BINGO deliverable D3.1, version 2.0, pre-processing and denoising (https://bingo-project.gr/download/397), read 2026-10-12
delivered_signal.note: as the project states it; not re-verified against the delivered file

project_reported.kind: reported by the BINGO project on its other dataset; not run here and not comparable with the results above
project_reported.dataset: the project’s NATO-alphabet inner-speech dataset: 20 participants, 26 words, three sessions
project_reported.reading: the deliverable reports performance at chance level for people the model was not trained on

bingo-cross-language.reading: Every direction is close to the 15-class prior of 6.67%, with each interval holding it, and top-3 accuracy is close to its 20% prior. The cross-language-minus-within-language contrast is small and its interval spans zero. A negative result for this baseline in this setting: it does not show that inner speech cannot be decoded by other methods.
limitations: One fixed spectral baseline: no EEG foundation model, PEFT or deep model was evaluated.
Source-defined subject fields are the operational groups; biological identity and cross-day grouping were not independently certified.

The delivered signals were already cleaned by the project (ASR and FORCe on the continuous recordings, by its own account); physical amplitude units, the named montage and the measured display latency are not established.
The nominal window was verified against the stored time vectors; that does not certify causal or online processing, brain-only signal origin, full BINGO coverage or cross-day performance.

The intervals are approximate and descriptive: fixed overlapping leave-one-field-out fits, no refit variability, not calibrated population confidence intervals. The shuffles measure sensitivity to the training labels and are not a calibrated randomization test.
The contrast is not superiority, equivalence, a significance test or a reliable transfer gain.
release_limits: Source-defined subject fields are the operational groups; biological identity and cross-day grouping were not independently certified.
Delivered signal preprocessing, physical amplitude units, named montage and measured display latency are not established.
The nominal action window was verified against stored time vectors; this does not certify causal or online processing.
The partial nine-trial field is excluded by the prospective complete-record rule; no score-driven exclusions.
No EEG foundation model, PEFT or deep model was evaluated in this pilot.
Approximate descriptive bootstrap intervals condition on overlapping leave-one-field-out fits and omit training-refit variability.
claims_not_supported: not evidence that inner speech cannot be decoded
no superiority or equivalence between languages, and no significance test
no online, real-time or brain-only decoding claim
not a foundation-model ranking, and no medical or diagnostic claim

independent_audit.not_checked: the 680 shuffle models were reconstructed, not refitted, and the raw file was not re-extracted: the audit used cached features and verified lineage receipts

handwriting-mask-aware.title: Mask-aware EEG: a five-person development diagnostic
handwriting-mask-aware.question: When channels that sit flat at a digital rail are masked, what is left, and does it predict four released labels better than the masks and the clock do?
handwriting-mask-aware.task: four released coded labels, 0 to 3 (events 200 to 203), from a fixed window 0.5–4.5 seconds after the released EEG-relative onset; glyph identity and continuous trajectories are not established, so this is not handwriting recognition

cohort.reuse: a reused development cohort: the same five training people as the earlier analysis, whose scores were seen before this design; not a new or independent cohort
cohort.split: five leave-one-person-out folds; every session of the held-out person excluded from fitting
cohort.official_test: the official ten-person test signals and reference labels were not used; earlier intake inspected unlabeled test metadata, and this analysis made no further test access

handwriting-mask-aware.weighting: the unweighted mean of the five held-out people’s balanced accuracy

relative_eeg.label: Mask-aware relative EEG
relative_eeg.description: 295 channel-major relative Welch band-power slots from the available channels, zero where a channel is unavailable

mask_only.label: Missingness mask only
mask_only.description: 59 availability bits plus the available-channel fraction
mask_only.interval_note: not published: with five people, this control’s bootstrap bounds would show individual people’s scores

time_only.label: Elapsed time / trial order
time_only.description: onset, log1p(onset), trial rank and rank over count

mask_plus_time.label: Mask + time
mask_plus_time.description: the mask and time controls together

majority.label: Training-majority control
majority.description: the most frequent class of the four training people

relative_eeg_minus_mask_only.label: Relative EEG minus missingness mask only

relative_eeg_minus_time_only.label: Relative EEG minus elapsed time / trial order

relative_eeg.range_is: the lowest and highest replicate means: an observed range, not a confidence interval

mask_only.range_is: the lowest and highest replicate means: an observed range, not a confidence interval

time_only.range_is: the lowest and highest replicate means: an observed range, not a confidence interval

mask_plus_time.range_is: the lowest and highest replicate means: an observed range, not a confidence interval

label_shuffle.design: five fixed training-label shuffles per representation, preserving source person and session; sensitivity controls, not a full permutation significance test

availability.flags_note: the constant and lower-rail flags overlap and must not be summed
availability.available_means: nonconstant, not touching either header-declared digital rail and numerically valid under a fixed rule: not certified clean physiological EEG
availability.scope: counts for the selected cohort only, not the whole source dataset

earlier_analysis.relation: the same five people, sessions and trials, analysed earlier with all-channel common-average referencing and log band power: context, not a second cohort
earlier_analysis.not_attributable: masking, referencing and the spectral representation changed together, so the difference between the two analyses cannot be attributed to masking, and no best model is selected from them

method.window: 0.5–4.5 seconds after the released EEG-relative onset: 4,000 samples at 1,000 Hz; only the 59 header-identified EEG channels read
method.masking: constant, rail-touching or nonfinite channel-windows masked before any transform; available channels demeaned individually; no common-average reference and no interpolation
method.inputs: Welch estimates (1,000-sample Hann window, 500 overlap); five half-open bands from 1 to 45 Hz, each divided by the sum of the five
method.model: source-only standardization and balanced multinomial logistic regression, C=1, lbfgs, max_iter 2000, tolerance 1e-4, seed 20261012
method.sealing: all 125 checkpoints sealed before the separate scorer opened held-out truth

uncertainty.kind: descriptive 2.5–97.5% intervals from 10,000 fixed-seed person-bootstrap draws over five people
uncertainty.conditional_on: the already fitted overlapping folds: not calibrated population confidence intervals or evidence of superiority

handwriting-mask-aware.reading: Mask-aware relative EEG is slightly above the 25% majority control, and above the missingness-only and mask-plus-time controls with paired intervals above zero; against the elapsed-time control the paired interval crosses zero. Five people and four coded labels: a data-quality and methods case study, not handwriting recognition.
limitations: Five reused development people whose earlier scores were seen before this design: no independent confirmation and no population inference.
Four released coded labels: glyph identity and trajectories are not established, so this is not handwriting recognition.
Availability is a numerical rule, not certified clean EEG; why other channels sit flat at a digital rail is unknown.
Masking, referencing and the spectral representation changed together, so no difference from the earlier analysis can be attributed to masking.
The contrast with the elapsed-time control crosses zero.
Optical species, units and the clock between modalities are unresolved, so no fNIRS or fusion conclusion follows; no online, physiological-origin, competition-standing or medical claim.

Audit scope: all 120 stored models reconstructed and the 20 true-label models refitted independently, with no discrepancy; the shuffle models were not refitted, and the audit used cached derived artifacts, not fresh raw-feature extraction.
claims_not_supported: not handwriting recognition and not glyph or trajectory decoding
no superiority over the elapsed-time control
no fNIRS, fusion, online, competition-standing or medical claim
not a leaderboard entry or a model recommendation

independent_audit.not_checked: the raw samples were not reread and the features were not re-extracted

refed-stored-clip.title: REFED: a stored-clip computational diagnostic
refed-stored-clip.question: Can whole-clip EEG band power predict a clip’s mean self-reported valence and arousal better than simple source-only controls?

eeg_ridge.description: 320 relative Welch band powers per clip (five bands at each of 64 channel positions), source-only standardization, Ridge with alpha 1

duration_video_id_ridge.label: Duration / numeric-video-ID Ridge
duration_video_id_ridge.description: Ridge on stored duration and the numeric video ID, a key-index proxy and not established presentation order

conditions.label: Shared videos, held folder
conditions.design: two folds: train on all 15 clips of one folder and predict the other folder; familiar stimuli can support prediction through stimulus identity

conditions.label: Jointly held folder and video IDs
conditions.design: ten folds: each folder held out with one of five fixed three-video groups, training on the other folder’s 12 remaining videos

refed-stored-clip.controls_lesson: With shared videos, the lookup of the same video’s training target has the smallest error: familiar stimuli can carry the prediction through stimulus identity, which is why that control is there. When folder and video are held out together the lookup has no matching video and falls back to the global mean, so the two are equal. This illustrates the confound; it does not establish a mechanism.

quality.note: finite, nonconstant values and valid spectral denominators in every clip: numerical eligibility only, not acquisition quality, physical units or physiological specificity

uncertainty.kind: none: no confidence interval or significance test, because two nominal folders support no population inference

method.inputs: five relative Welch band powers, [1,4), [4,8), [8,13), [13,30) and [30,45) Hz, each divided by that channel’s [1,45) Hz total, for each of the 64 original channel positions: 320 per clip; Welch at the nominal 1,000 Hz with one-second Hann windows and 50% overlap
method.model: source-only standardization and Ridge with fixed alpha 1, no tuning; predictions finite but unclipped, no calibration after the fact
method.channels: no channel selection, common-average reference, cross-channel mixing or invented trim
method.sealing: all fold predictions and fitted parameters sealed before separate scoring

refed-stored-clip.reading: EEG Ridge has a larger error than every source-only control in both conditions. With shared videos, the same-video lookup has the smallest error; when folder and video are held out together, the lookup has no matching video and equals the global mean. No physiological or population claim follows.
limitations: Two nominal folders and 15 shared video keys: a descriptive computational diagnostic, not a population, cross-day or leaderboard result.

Stored EEG units, calibration and sensor validity, the precise EEG-to-label clock and the annotation polling are unresolved; relative band power removes a constant channel gain, which is a property of the representation only.
Published video durations exceed the stored arrays by two seconds and the crop end points are unknown: pairing whole arrays establishes no precise physiological alignment.
The numeric video ID is a key-index proxy, not established presentation order, and the shared-video condition carries familiar-stimulus confounding.
The label vectors had been inspected, all 30 means computed privately and two arrays quality-checked before this design: these are not untouched targets.
No confidence interval, significance test, clinical affect, neural specificity or population claim.
release_limits: Two nominal source groups and shared15video keys support descriptive computational diagnostics only; clips are not30independent people.
